title: Quit India Movement
definition: A mass civil disobedience movement launched by the Indian National Congress on August 8, 1942, demanding an orderly British withdrawal from India, characterized by the slogan 'Do or Die'.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the final major mass struggle before independence, testing candidates on the shift from constitutional agitation to spontaneous mass uprising and the role of underground activities.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Quit India Movement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Rise of Left-wing influence in INC
